summary: Round 2 launch-readiness review of the verified-copy stage at 1082075619d1. All round-1 findings are addressed. S1 (blocking) is resolved. stage.sbatch resolves the attempt and bundle with realpath -e. It requires the attempt to be under the campaign root, the bundle to be attempt/bundle, and pwd -P to equal the attempt. Slurm --chdir, --output and --error are pinned to attempt01. noclobber is set, datasets must be absent, and `mkdir job-started` fails if the attempt is reused, all before any evidence is written. stage.py also requires the resolved output to be inside the campaign root. S2: posix_fadvise DONTNEED runs after fsync, and the receipt says cache residency and remote bytes are unverified. S3: TERM@120 plus a SIGTERM handler writes the failed state before raising. The 2 h limit stays, with a provisional 30-90 min ETA that is refined after each verified set. S4: six main() tests cover 6-set/30-copy success, an injected set-2 failure (failed status, no complete.json, partial sets retained), reuse, bad manifest, outside-campaign output and a mismatched pin. S5: the five native getstripe sections in evidence.txt parse to OSTs 273/106/76/91/92. S6: the manifest SHA256 is pinned. It matches the coordinator's independent sha256sum, and the manifest holds exactly five bd rows with the expected names. test-log.txt shows 17 tests OK; the MUNGE warning after OK is an environment message. One new low, non-blocking robustness note (S7) about SIGTERM handling. The code is ready to launch within the agreed scope (first six sets, one lcls_g premium node). Native acceptance is not claimed. It needs the job's 30 receipts, complete.json, unchanged source identities and Slurm accounting, reviewed in the final round.

The SIGTERM handler calls update() and save(), which reuse the same status.json.tmp path. If the signal lands while the main thread is inside save(), the handler truncates and renames the tmp file. The interrupted outer stream then flushes into the renamed inode while it unwinds, which could leave status.json malformed. Separately, the RuntimeError raised inside the `with ThreadPoolExecutor` block triggers shutdown(wait=True). Queued copy/hash tasks therefore keep running until SIGKILL, and the except-branch update may never run. The failed state is still written first and complete.json cannot appear, so the gating holds.
findings.requested_change: Optional. In the handler, set a flag or write to a distinct temp name, e.g. include the pid/a counter in the tmp suffix. Consider pool.shutdown(cancel_futures=True) on failure. When reviewing an interrupted run, treat Slurm accounting and the absence of complete.json as authoritative.
